subject: QMon: handoff + eval harness integration / canary & rollback thresholds (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: QMon: handoff + eval harness integration / canary & rollback thresholds (Acme Health)

Hi Sarah (and James),

Congrats on getting to the implementation window — excited to get Quality Monitoring (QMon) set up for your ACME-Clinical Notes workflow. To make the kickoff efficient, I wanted to surface the proposed scope and ask for confirmation on a few items before the 9/16 kickoff: 

High-level scope (what Redwood will help stand up):
- Prompt sets for priority intents (diagnosis extraction, medication normalization, sensitive redaction). Attached: QMon_AcmePromptSet_v1.csv as a starting set.
- Eval harness integration: nightly batch eval + continuous canary runs on a 1% traffic slice. See attached spec (eval-harness-integration-spec.pdf).
- Regression alerts: slack/email alerts for >5% drop in top-line pass rate or >8% drift in per-intent F1 across rolling 7d baseline.
- Canary/rollback policy: automatic rollback to previous model variant if canary pass rate < 90% or latency degradation >20% vs baseline for 10 minutes.

Questions for you before kickoff: 
1) Is the 1% live traffic canary acceptable or do you prefer a synthetic-only canary?
2) Who on your side owns the final prompt review (labeling / edge-case examples)? We need a point of contact for rapid clarifications during onboarding.
3) Any constraints around sending de-identified snippets to Redwood for nightly evals? (We can also run the evals inside your VPC if needed.)

Next steps: If you confirm the above, I’ll schedule a 45-min kickoff on 9/16 and loop in the implementation engineer and CS lead. I’ve linked the drive folder with the prompt CSV and the integration spec.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0179

Attachments: QMon_AcmePromptSet_v1.csv (sample prompt set), eval-harness-integration-spec.pdf (integration checklist)
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Carter <james.carter@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QMon: handoff + eval harness integration / canary & rollback thresholds (Acme Health)

Thanks Vanessa — this looks good and very thorough. A few quick answers: 

- Canary: We prefer to start synthetic-only for the first two weeks (data governance team wants to sign off on sending any production-derived snippets). After that, we can move to a 0.5% live traffic canary.
- Prompt review owner: James will own the prompt set review and provide edge-case examples by 9/15.
- Data constraints: We cannot send any PHI offsite. If Redwood needs realistic samples for the eval harness, we will either (a) run the eval inside our VPC, or (b) provide fully de-identified, human-reviewed examples.

Can you confirm whether the nightly batch eval can run inside our VPC (we use AWS, us-west-2)? If not, please describe the de-identification requirements.

—Sarah
Sarah Li
Director of Clinical Informatics | Acme Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QMon: handoff + eval harness integration / canary & rollback thresholds (Acme Health)

Great — thanks for the quick clarifications. Short answers: 

- Running evals inside your VPC: yes, Redwood Private can run the nightly eval harness in your AWS us-west-2 account. We’ll need minimal IAM read-only access to the S3 bucket with the de-id fixtures or we can deploy a small Lambda-based eval runner if you prefer no cross-account access. I’ve noted: IMPLEMENTATION: VPC eval option.

- Canary plan update: we’ll switch to synthetic-only for the first 14 days, then a 0.5% live canary (ramping to 1% over 7 days) after sign-off. I’m attaching a draft canary thresholds spreadsheet (canary-thresholds.xlsx) with proposed metrics.

- Prompt ownership: thanks James for taking point. Lauren, Marissa — can one of you own the prompt ingestion + mapping into the eval harness? Suggested pre-kickoff work: ingest the attached CSV into our eval format and flag any prompts needing clarification.

Proposed kickoff agenda (45 minutes):
1) Introductions & roles (5m)
2) Review prompt set & examples (10m)
3) Eval harness options (VPC vs Redwood-hosted) and security controls (10m)
4) Canary/rollback policy and thresholds (10m)
5) Next steps & timeline (10m)

I’ll schedule the meeting for 9/16 10:00am PT unless you suggest otherwise.

—Vanessa
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-13T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QMon: handoff + eval harness integration / canary & rollback thresholds (Acme Health)

Sarah / team — happy to take prompt ingestion. Quick operational checklist from CS/implementation perspective: 

Pre-kickoff (due 9/15):
- Receive final prompt CSV (James) — will validate formatting against eval harness schema.
- Confirm de-id approach (VPC eval vs de-id fixtures). If VPC: request minimal IAM role and S3 path.
- Prepare mapping: intent name -> canonical label, acceptance criteria (pass/fail rules), and sample edge cases.

Kickoff deliverables (within 2 business days after kickoff):
- Imported prompt set in eval harness (tagged by intent)
- Baseline nightly eval run (0-day) with pass/fail rates and a short report
- Canary run config created (synthetic only) with monitoring dashboards, alerts, and rollback policy encoded into rollout recipe.

Canary / rollback specifics (operational):
- Canary metric set: top-line pass rate, per-intent F1, average latency (p95).
- Hold/back criteria (will abort rollout): top-line pass rate < 90% OR any intent F1 drop > 8% vs baseline.
- Latency rollback: sustained p95 > baseline * 1.20 for 10 minutes triggers automatic rollback.
- Escalation path: if auto-rollback triggers, the on-call engineer (Rishi) and CS lead (Marissa) are paged; product owner (Vanessa) and Sarah are notified.

Let me know if you want me to add these items into the kickoff agenda doc.

—Lauren
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QMon: handoff + eval harness integration / canary & rollback thresholds (Acme Health)

Adding a couple engineering notes on the canary & regression alerts: 

- Canary rollout: we’ll create a model-variant tag for this rollout and wire up continuous small-batch evaluation every 5 minutes against the synthetic canary set. If the synthetic canary passes, the system will proceed with the 0.5% live ramp (per Sarah’s preference).
- Regression alerts: Redwood Optimize can monitor token-level cost deltas and output-quality deltas. We’ll configure two alert channels: Slack (#acme-qmon-alerts) + email to the distro list. Alert thresholds to start: 5% top-line pass drop OR a 10% token-cost per inference increase.
- Playbook for an auto-rollback: snapshot current model variant -> deploy candidate -> run canary -> if criteria fail, automatic revert to snapshot + incident ticket auto-created in Jira (SUP-ACME-xxxx).

I’ll provision the canary job and a temp Slack channel before kickoff so CS and Acme can validate alerts during the synthetic phase.

—Rishi
Staff Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
